summary: Full e2e verification of the hierarchical İş Kolları (Task Categories) feature — parent/child/grandchild creation, unlimited depth, per-node colors, expand/collapse chevron, rename, cascade delete, and filter chip breadcrumb rendering. Backend pytest suite (5/5 passed) covers create parent→child→grandchild with parent_id chain, per-(company,parent) duplicate uniqueness, invalid parent, cascade delete (subtree removed + tasks' category_id cleared without deleting tasks), and assignment to any depth. Frontend UI verified 12/15 checks passing — the 3 non-passes are (a) admin-serkan has no company_id so scope=my_tasks category filter chips do not surface for the newly-created categories (pre-existing scope behavior, NOT a regression from this feature), (b) task-category-select is only rendered inside a create/edit task modal (not the main page — expected), and (c) the UI cascade-delete triggers a custom confirm modal (not window.confirm) so the auto-accept-dialog hook did not confirm; verified separately via API DELETE that returned {deleted:true,count:3}. All test data cleaned up.

integration_issues.flow: Task filter chips for hierarchical categories (admin without company_id)
integration_issues.issue: Categories created under Test Company A do NOT appear as filter chips in serkan's tasks panel because backend /api/task-categories?scope=my_tasks filters strictly by (user.company_id OR visible_to lists). Since admin serkan has no company_id, none of the created categories match and chips are hidden. This makes the breadcrumb-in-chip scenario un-verifiable via the primary admin account. NOT a regression, but users may expect admin-without-company to still see chips or a company picker in the tasks panel.

action_items: Optional: consider surfacing hierarchical filter chips for admin users without a company_id (currently the my_tasks scope returns empty for such users, so chips never appear). Not a regression of this feature — pre-existing scope behavior.
UI cascade-delete uses a custom confirm modal; if automated cleanup is desired, expose data-testid on the confirm/OK button so tests can click it.
Note: Login response returns 'token' (not 'access_token'); the /app/memory/test_credentials.md was accurate but any new tests should use r.json()['token'].
critical_code_review_comments: Backend routers/tasks_router.py is 1600+ lines — consider extracting the task-categories block (create/patch/delete + hierarchy validation) into a small tasks_categories_router.py; models are already split, keeping the router file coherent.

Frontend TasksPanel.jsx is 2300+ lines — hard to review; the category-filter chip block (~1690-1750) is a good candidate for a <CategoryChipBar/> subcomponent that receives orderedCategories + categoryCounts + selection callbacks.

categoryTree.getCategoryPath has a cycle-guard via a Set — good; buildForest/flattenTree have no cycle guard but rely on parent_id being non-cyclic which the backend enforces at create-time (no cycle-check for MOVE — however there is no move endpoint yet, so this is fine).

Backend cascade delete performs an in-memory graph traversal across ALL categories of the company (up to length=5000); acceptable at current scale but consider using MongoDB $graphLookup if categories per company grow > ~1000.

success_rate.frontend: 80% (12/15 UI checks — the 3 misses are not regressions)

seed_data_creation: Created QA2UI74302_R (root, +alt color), QA2UI74302_C (child), QA2UI74302_GX (grandchild) under 'Test Company A'. All 3 removed via cascade DELETE at teardown (verified count=3 via API). No leftover state.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Hierarchy backend endpoints are solid — reuse /app/backend/tests/test_task_category_hierarchy.py. UI test flow: (1) settings-tab-categories requires selecting a company via category-company-picker before create works (React onChange must fire — use native setter + change event). Test Company A id: d2d294a2-9266-4f3b-afaf-50dbb55088ca. (2) UI delete of category uses a custom confirm modal — window.dialog listener won't help; find the modal's Yes/OK button. (3) Filter chips (category-chip-{name}) only appear when the user has a matching company_id — admin serkan has no company_id, so create categories under a company the tester impersonates OR just verify via API + a company-scoped user for chip UI.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature works as designed. The 3 UI checks that didn't complete are due to (a) admin without company_id + my_tasks scope filtering, (b) a modal-only component, and (c) custom confirm modal, not to a bug in the hierarchy feature.
